title: Underived continuous functions compute derived internal functions of profinite parameters
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$ and a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with its extending norm topology. Put $F=E$ and $A_F(S)=C(S,F)$ with all continuous functions [def-sfb-continuous-map-condensed-ring]. Use the small coherent profinite site in [def-weil-size-convention], its ordinary internal $A_F$-modules [sk-def-sfb-module-objects], and ordinary derived categories [sk-def-sfb-derived-categories]. For a profinite set $P$ in these universes, let $A_F[P]$ be the free internal $A_F$-module on $\underline P(S)=C(S,P)$; this is the left adjoint to forgetting modules to condensed sets. Let $\mathcal C_F(P)$ be the internal module whose sections on $S$ are $C(S\times P,F)$, with $A_F(S)$ acting through the $S$-coordinate. Evaluation identifies it with $\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}_{A_F}(A_F[P],A_F)$, where internal module Hom is the right adjoint of internal tensor. Derive this Hom in its second variable by nonnegative injective resolutions. The canonical resolution comparison is an isomorphism
$$\mathcal C_F(P)[0]\longrightarrow R\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}_{A_F}(A_F[P],A_F[0])$$
in $D(\operatorname{Mod}_{A_F})$. It is natural contravariantly in every continuous map of profinite parameter sets and its degree-zero map is the evaluation identification just specified. The coefficient field $F=E$ is complete. All continuous functions are retained; no restriction to locally constant functions is imposed.

proof.text: Use [lem-sfb-profinite-free-hom-resolution-evaluation] and transport its normalized evaluation to the chosen adjoint model using [lem-sfb-profinite-actual-free-hom-evaluation]. At the regular coefficient module this is exactly the counit-defined evaluation in the statement, followed by ULift.down. The additive natural isomorphism gives bijectivity and additivity. Its scalar law, the multiplication-extension equation for the continuous ring sheaf, and its two restriction laws give the stated scalar action and both pointwise restriction formulas.

source.place: Tag 03EO, lemma-internal-hom-adjoint-tensor; free-generator normalization in parent proof steps 1 and 3.

proof.text: Completeness follows from finite dimensionality over the complete field Q_ell. For any injective resolution I, [lem-sfb-finite-normed-scalar-section-acyclicity] gives that its evaluated augmentation at each V is a quasi-isomorphism: degree zero is its asserted isomorphism; in positive degree both homologies are zero. Apply this with V=S times P and conjugate by the additive natural evaluation isomorphism from step 1. This proves that every section evaluation of resolutionAugmentation is a quasi-isomorphism. Forget the module structure, regard the resulting map as a presheaf map of complexes, use sectionwise detection of quasi-isomorphisms, and apply exact sheafification. The sheafification counit identifies the result with the original sheaf map. The exact conservative module forgetful functor then reflects the quasi-isomorphism. Extension from natural to integer degrees preserves quasi-isomorphisms, and derived localization makes it invertible.

proof.text: Take any injective resolution I of the regular module. Step 2 also says that applying H_P to its augmentation is a quasi-isomorphism. Extend to integer degrees and use the natural map/extension isomorphisms to deduce the same for H_P applied to I.iota-prime. Naturality of the ordinary right-derived unit gives a square with this map on the left, the derived image of I.iota-prime on the right, and the unit at the bounded-below injective complex I at the bottom. These three maps are invertible; hence the unit at the single regular module is invertible. Its specified single-complex normalization differs only by an isomorphism. The parameter naturality square for nonnegative augmentations is checked degreewise: degree zero is naturality of parameterMap at I.iota.f 0; every other degree has zero source. The canonical degree-zero identity is the already proved rightDerivedSingleUnit_zero formula.
